title: Unified Control policies (Release B, BAUPLAN v1.1 §7)
description: Policy documents per hierarchy level (org -> workspace -> vault -> instance), their effective merge and the signed per-instance bundle. Every member has `x-merge` (its merge rule = tightening direction: union = deny wins, intersection = allowed values every level allows, groups = every allowlist must match, min = stricter limit, true_wins/false_wins, rank = later enum value is stricter, equal = levels must agree else non_mergeable) and `x-enforcement`: `instance` = enforced by the instance's gateway policy pack field `x-instance`, `server` = enforced by Cloud itself at the point `x-server` names (403 policy_denied {member, level}), whatever the instance does, `advisory` = distributed and shown, not enforced yet. Enforcement covers access through LeanCTX only.

level.description: hierarchy level, outermost first; lower levels can only tighten

agent_name.description: An agent: a name such as claude-code, codex, cursor or acp:<id>, or '*' alone for every agent.

check_name.description: A check's name as the host's project configures it: the record's check-name form (cloud-record-0.3 `checks`) without `/`, so a path never passes for a check.

readable_root.description: A readable folder: starts with '{project}', '~' or '/', has no '..' part and compiles as a glob.

excluded_paths.description: Path globs (gitignore style) whose content never enters context or shared knowledge.
excluded_paths.x-server: a push, task result, draft or code graph with a code anchor path the globs match is refused

block_secrets.description: Block agent writes and actions that carry detected secrets or PII.

pii.description: PII detector action on inbound content; redact = anonymise.

allowed_models.description: Model allowlists (glob-lite, '*' wildcard): a model is allowed when it matches a pattern of every group; an empty group allows no model.

external_model_excluded_classes.description: Data classes that are never sent to an external (remote) model.

confidential_out_of_sharing.description: Keep content classified confidential out of team sharing.

blocked_model_origins.description: Countries of origin whose model weights are never used (catalog origin_country), whatever the host.

blocked_host_countries.description: Countries where no model request is processed (catalog host_country, including vendors' own APIs).

vendor_direct_cn.description: Allow instances to opt in to a vendor's own API processed in CN; false forbids it.

allowed_providers.description: Model providers (e.g. anthropic, openai, google, mistral) whose APIs agents may reach; a provider outside every setting level's list is refused. An empty list allows none. Hosts from the next LeanCTX release enforce it; each Host's policy acknowledgement says whether it does (older Hosts report it as not enforced).

readable_roots.description: Folders agents may read (glob patterns starting with '{project}' for the project root, '~' for the home folder or '/'); anything outside every setting level's list stays unreadable. Levels meet by folder containment: where one folder holds another, the narrower one stays. An empty list allows none.

never_send.description: Path globs (gitignore style) whose content is never sent to a model, whatever reads it.

require_proxy.description: Model traffic of agents goes only through the LeanCTX proxy: a model request not routed through it is refused. Hosts that do not enforce it yet report it in their ack's unenforced.

agents.description: Rules for agents (ent2); optional, absent when no level sets a member of it.

allowed.description: Agents that may work (claude-code, codex, cursor, acp:<id>, …); '*' alone allows every agent and yields to any list. An empty list allows none. Hosts from the next LeanCTX release enforce it; each Host's policy acknowledgement says whether it does (older Hosts report it as not enforced). Matched against the name an agent gives in the MCP handshake, which an agent can spoof: a guide, not a security boundary.

agents_effective.description: Rules for agents (ent2) of the effective policy; present only when a level sets a member of it.

orchestrator.description: Rules for Orchestrators on the vault's agent bus (QN2); optional, absent when no level sets a member of it.

network.description: The Orchestrator network of the vault's agent bus: false = an Orchestrator neither posts nor relays Orchestrator messages for the vault and stays local. Absent = allowed.

cross_team_review.description: Review across people: false = an Orchestrator neither asks an Orchestrator on another person's host to review work in the vault nor reviews theirs. Absent = allowed. Not enforced by Hosts yet.

max_sessions_per_vault.description: At most this many sessions started by Orchestrators run at once for the vault on one host; the next start is refused. 0 = an Orchestrator starts no session there. Absent = no cap. Not enforced by Hosts yet.

orchestrator_effective.description: Rules for Orchestrators (QN2) of the effective policy; present only when a level sets a member of it.

landing.description: How the team's own host lands changes on trunk (Landing); optional, absent when no level sets a member of it. The host reads the org and workspace merge from GET /api/v1/host/policy.

require_approval.description: Every change needs an approval on the forge before the host lands it. Absent = the host's own setting.

required_checks.description: Checks (by the name the host's project configures) that must pass before a change lands; every setting level's checks apply. Absent = the host's own checks.

revert_on_regression.description: A landed change that breaks trunk (a real failure, not an infrastructure problem or timeout) is reverted by the host. Absent = the host's own setting.

max_parallel.description: At most this many changes are checked and landed together. Absent = the host's own limit.

landing_effective.description: Landing rules of the effective policy; present only when a level sets a member of it.

document.description: one level's policy document (W routes); every member optional, absent = this level adds no rule; at most 8 KiB canonical JSON

effective.description: merge of at most one document per level, in normal form: security, context and sharing present (agents, orchestrator and landing each only when a level sets a member of it), every set sorted ascending (bytewise), groups sorted, absent member = no level sets it

source.description: a document that went into the bundle: org/workspace scope = org_id (an organisation's org-level document: orgn_ + its id), vault = vault id, instance = instance_id

bundle.description: signed effective policy of one instance (purpose key `policy` of key set v3): Ed25519 over "leanctx.cloud.effective-policy.v1\n" || canonical_json(bundle without signature), signature lowercase hex. `version` grows strictly per instance; an instance refuses a lower version or the same version with another digest (downgrade), a bundle for another org_id/instance_id, and treats it as expired after not_after (sensitive actions fail closed, the last valid rules keep restricting local work).

effective.description: org ∧ workspace ∧ instance: applies to every vault without an entry in `vaults`

vaults.description: per vault with a vault-level document: org ∧ workspace ∧ vault ∧ instance, ascending by vault_id

digest.description: digest of `policy`; the instance acks it

bundle_response.description: GET /v1/policy/bundle for Cloud-Protocol 2.x: the schema, the filter packs and `effective_policy` (null only when this server has no lease signing key); no TOML org policy members

ack_request.description: POST /v1/policy/ack: the instance applied this bundle; `unenforced` lists the members this instance cannot enforce (`x-enforcement: instance`); server-enforced members are never listed. With `refused`: the instance received this bundle (`version`, `digest` as received) but refused it and keeps applying the bundle `refused.applied_version` (null: it holds no valid bundle); `unenforced` is then absent

detail.description: the instance's diagnostic line, no content

refusal_reason.description: why an instance refused a received bundle: invalid_bundle (does not parse or validate), wrong_target (issued for another org or instance), key_unavailable (no verified key set v3 or no valid policy key for key_id), signature_invalid, digest_mismatch (digest is not the policy's), downgrade (older version, or the same version with another digest), expired (not_after already passed), install_failed (verified but could not be stored)

state.description: outdated: a newer bundle was issued to this instance since

ack_refused_response.description: POST /v1/policy/ack answer to a refusal (`refused` in the request): recorded; the normal ack answer is ack_response

exchange_kind.description: A bus message kind another agent receives (progress is always allowed).
